text: SMCS Constitution Article VII states that a majority of voting BoG members constitutes a quorum and proxy is not counted in determining quorum.
Synthetic Governance Procedure GP-07 (2025) states that one-third of voting BoG members constitutes a quorum and that submitted proxies count toward quorum.

A committee briefing note discusses board of governors quorum in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Constitution Article VII states that proxy voting is not allowed.
Synthetic Remote Meeting Guide RMG-02 (2026) permits each absent BoG member to appoint one voting proxy for ordinary business.

A committee briefing note discusses proxy voting in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Bylaws Article II requires each member to be notified of the time and place of a BoG meeting at least 20 days before the scheduled meeting.
Synthetic Secretariat Checklist SC-11 (2025) says routine BoG meetings require only 10 calendar days of notice.

A committee briefing note discusses bog meeting notice in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Constitution Article XI allows initiation by a petition signed by 5 percent of SMCS members or by a two-thirds vote of the entire voting BoG.
Synthetic Amendment Quick Guide AQG-1 (2026) says a petition from 3 percent of members is sufficient to initiate a constitutional amendment.

A committee briefing note discusses constitution amendment initiation in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Constitution Article XI states that notice of a proposed Bylaw change must be sent to each BoG member at least two weeks before action.
Synthetic Governance FAQ GF-04 (2025) says seven days of advance notice is sufficient for a Bylaw change.

A committee briefing note discusses bylaw amendment notice in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Constitution Article V states that a Member-at-Large serves a three-year term.
Synthetic Board Handbook BH-09 (2026) describes Members-at-Large as serving two-year terms.

A committee briefing note discusses member-at-large term in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Bylaws Article I states that the President serves a two-calendar-year term.
Synthetic Officer Transition Memo OTM-3 (2026) states that the President serves a single three-year term.

A committee briefing note discusses president term in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.

SMCS Bylaws Article I requires Vice President candidates to have been voting BoG members elected by the membership-at-large during the past five calendar years and to have served at least one full year by nomination.
Synthetic Election FAQ EF-8 (2025) says any Senior Member of SMCS with five years of Society membership may stand for Vice President without prior BoG service.

A committee briefing note discusses vice president eligibility in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Bylaws Article I states that candidates for President and President-Elect must have served at least one year as a Vice President.
Synthetic Leadership Succession Guide LSG-2 (2026) says two years as a Member-at-Large is an acceptable substitute for Vice President service.

A committee briefing note discusses president-elect eligibility in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Bylaws Article I requires a petition signed by at least 2 percent of SMCS members for additional Member-at-Large nominations.
Synthetic Election Operations Note EON-12 (2025) sets the petition threshold at 1 percent.

A committee briefing note discusses petition nomination threshold in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Technical Committee Manual states that each TC must propose at least one special session at the annual SMC conference.
Synthetic TC Flexibility Memo TCF-6 (2026) states that proposing a special session is optional if the TC organizes a webinar.

A committee briefing note discusses technical committee special session in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Technical Committee Manual states that all TC Chairs and Co-Chairs must be SMCS members.
Synthetic External Collaboration Guide ECG-4 (2025) permits a non-SMCS industry expert to serve as sole TC Chair for up to two years.

A committee briefing note discusses tc chair membership in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Technical Committee Manual requires TC Chairs to report activities bi-annually to the corresponding Area VP.
Synthetic TC Reporting Standard TRS-10 (2026) requires only one annual report.

A committee briefing note discusses tc activity reporting in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Technical Committee Manual says a TC may be discontinued if inactive for at least one year with no credible revival plan.
Synthetic TC Lifecycle Procedure TCLP-3 (2025) permits automatic dissolution after six months of inactivity.

A committee briefing note discusses tc dissolution inactivity period in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Technical Committee Manual requires a request to the Area VP, Area Committee review for activity plan and overlap, and Area VP approval before activity begins.
Synthetic Innovation Fast-Track IFT-1 (2026) allows a proposed TC to begin immediately after submitting a request, before Area Committee review.

A committee briefing note discusses new tc approval in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
SMCS Constitution Article VIII states that SMCS shall sponsor or cosponsor at least one major technical conference each year.
Synthetic Cost-Control Directive CCD-5 (2026) says the Society may skip all major conference sponsorship for a year whenever reserves fall below an internal target.

A committee briefing note discusses annual conference sponsorship in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
Draft SMCS Operational Manual V5 states that a change in Society dues requires approval by two-thirds of all voting BoG members.
Synthetic Finance Desk Guide FDG-7 (2026) says a simple majority of voting members present may approve a dues change.

A committee briefing note discusses smcs dues approval in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
Draft SMCS Operational Manual V5 describes a three-year geographic rotation: Americas, Asia/Oceania, Europe/Africa.
Synthetic Conference Strategy 2026-2029 states a four-year rotation adding a separate Middle East region.

A committee briefing note discusses flagship conference rotation in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
IEEE Bylaws state that Life Member status requires age 65 and age plus years of IEEE membership equal to or greater than 100.
Synthetic Membership FAQ MF-22 (2026) says Life Member status begins automatically at age 65 regardless of years of membership.

A committee briefing note discusses ieee life member eligibility in general terms but does not state a binding threshold, eligibility rule, approval requirement, or exception. It directs readers to consult the applicable governing documents.
IEEE governance provisions describe a hierarchy in which organizational-unit manuals and policy statements must conform to higher-level IEEE governing documents.
Synthetic Local Autonomy Policy LAP-1 (2026) claims an SMCS operational manual may override an IEEE Bylaw when approved unanimously by the SMCS BoG.
